sections.html:
The office occupies the Courthouse Annex at 12 East Street, Pittsboro, in the ground-level wing facing the traffic circle where the historic Superior Courthouse stands. Parking is behind the annex, reached from Chatham Street (also US 15/501 South) just past the circle. From the lot, walk to the wide stairwell opening in the middle of the building, skip the stairs, and take the passage on the left to the end of the building nearest the BP station.

Send letters to P.O. Box 756, Pittsboro, NC 27312, and use the East Street address for courier deliveries. The main number is 919-542-8235.

Three different clocks apply here. Miss a cutoff and the package waits for the next business day.

  • Front counter: weekdays, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Paper documents: last accepted at 4:30 p.m.
  • Electronic submissions: taken between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

State holidays are closed days. Remaining 2026 closings are Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, and December 24, 25 and 28.

Recording a deed starts at $26.00 and covers 15 pages; each page after that adds $4.00. The $2 verification fee is built into that figure. Deeds of trust run $64 for the first 35 pages and also add $4 a page beyond that. Payment is due up front, before filing.

Chatham land record charges

Deed$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust$64 through page 35, then $4 a page

These match the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, which also tacks on $25.00 for a nonstandard document. Chatham lists a uniform commercial code filing at $38.00 for one or two pages.

Electronic filing runs through two vendors, Simplifile and CSC. The office takes those submissions Monday to Friday until 4:00 p.m., and it now e-records plats as well. Title companies and attorneys file this way as a matter of routine, so sellers rarely hand-carry anything.

CSC takes questions at erecording@cscglobal.com or 1-866-652-0111. A paper filing needs the original documents. The office stores records. It does not write documents or repair errors, so staff cannot draft or correct a deed for you.

Searching is a separate service. You can search recorded deeds at chathamncrod.org. The office also sends an e-mail alert whenever something is filed under a name you pick, a useful safeguard against deed fraud.

sections.h2: Formatting rules that can cost you $25
sections.html:
The layout in G.S. 161-14(b) applies to everything filed after July 1, 2002. A noncompliant document is still recorded, though the office first collects the $25.00 nonstandard fee, so clean formatting saves money. The requirements:

  • Standard letter or legal paper.
  • Page one needs an empty three-inch strip across the top, and every other edge needs a quarter inch of clear margin.
  • Dark ink on white paper, printed on one side, in type of at least 9 points.
  • The instrument type, such as warranty deed, printed just below that empty strip.
  • A prepared-by line on page one of each deed or deed of trust, outside the margin zones.
  • Where the original should be mailed back, written on page one of each paper filing.

Pen works for filling blanks on printed forms and for corrections.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
Sellers rarely handle this themselves, yet the sequence is worth knowing.

  1. An attorney prepares the deed with a prepared-by line and a return-to address on page one.
  2. The closing office checks the layout so the $25.00 nonstandard fee does not apply.
  3. Excise tax is deducted from the seller's proceeds and sent with the recording fee.
  4. The package goes in electronically before 4:00 p.m., or on paper before 4:30 p.m.
  5. Staff stamp the filing time. That time sets your place in line ahead of or behind any other filing on the property.

Late arrivals are not lost. They are stamped the following business day, so plan the closing hour accordingly.

sections.h2: Deed excise tax and recording priority
sections.html:
The state charges $1.00 for every $500 of price, rounded up, under G.S. 105-228.30. The seller owes it before the deed is recorded. Half stays with the county general fund, and the state revenue department gets the other half. Your closing attorney takes it out of your proceeds and forwards it with the recording package, so you will see it itemized on the settlement statement.

Filing order matters too. Under G.S. 47-18, a transfer offers no protection against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on file with the register of deeds where the land lies, and priority follows the time stamp. A buyer's lender wants the deed logged ahead of anything else filed against the house.

The county counts 38,294 housing units, and median home value for 2020 to 2024 was $446,200. At those prices the excise tax is a sizable closing cost here, so plan for it before you list.

The office also keeps births, deaths and marriages for the county and files notary oaths and assumed-name records. Marriage licenses and notary oaths require an appointment, made by calling 919-542-8235 as well.

Certified copies of birth and death records are $10.00 each, and a marriage license is $60.00. These records come up in sales more often than people expect. If you inherited the house, the title company will probably want a certified death certificate. A marriage or divorce may also change who has to sign. Order certified copies early. Only people eligible under state law can receive them.

Pay off the property tax, collect your paperwork, and leave recording to the closing office. Property is revalued every four years in Chatham, and the county rate held at 60 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-27, so the tax on your settlement statement may not match the bill you remember. For tax offices, appeals and relief programs, see our Chatham County property tax guide

If a mortgage is still open, get a payoff figure from the lender. Recording the cancellation costs nothing. Plat questions, old easements and missing signatures on inherited land should come up early, because the register of deeds cannot repair defects. Before listing, ask a North Carolina attorney how to clear any defect.

Selling for cash removes the lender's schedule, yet the deed still goes through this counter and these fees.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Pittsboro recording desk?
faqs.a: Dial 919-542-8235. Staff can answer questions about filing a package. The office is at 12 East Street, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 756.

faqs.q: What is the latest I can bring a paper deed to the Chatham counter?
faqs.a: Half past four on business days. Electronic filings cut off earlier, at four, and state holidays mean no recording at all.

faqs.q: What is the fee for an ordinary deed?
faqs.a: Budget $26.00 for a deed of up to fifteen pages, with $4.00 more for every added page. The excise tax the seller pays is a separate charge.

faqs.q: What if my deed ignores the layout rules?
faqs.a: The office will accept it and add $25.00 for a nonstandard document under G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Fix the top band and print dark on white before you submit.

faqs.q: Which electronic vendors does Chatham work with?
faqs.a: Simplifile and CSC. Both feed the register of deeds on weekdays up to 4:00 p.m., and plats can go in electronically too.
